nodes.summary: QQ adapter using the NoneBot (OneBot v11) protocol. Connect to a OneBot-compatible QQ client for sending messages. Actions: configure, send, status, call, block, unblock, allow, disallow.

action.description: configure | send | status | call | block | unblock | allow | disallow

url.description: OneBot HTTP API base URL (for configure)

nodes.summary: Start an HTTP server to receive OneBot v11 message events. Configure your OneBot client to POST events to http://<host>:<port>/onebot/event. Supports grayscale group whitelist.

agent_session_id.description: Optional: agent session ID for message routing

failure_modes: OneBot client not configured to POST events

nodes.summary: Start a WebSocket server to receive OneBot v11 message events via reverse WS connection. Configure your OneBot client (e.g. Napcat) to connect as a WebSocket client to ws://<host>:<port>/. Supports the same grayscale group whitelist as qq_serve.

action.description: Set to "stop" to shut down the WebSocket server and release the port

agent_session_id.description: Optional: agent session ID for message routing

side_effects: listens on configured port for OneBot WS client connections
failure_modes: OneBot WS client not configured to connect

nodes.summary: Fetch queued incoming QQ messages received by qq_serve. Returns all messages and drains the queue. Agent should poll this periodically.
Send a message to a QQ group or private chat via OneBot v11 HTTP API. Supports reply/quote via reply_to.
side_effects: sends HTTP request to OneBot API

nodes.summary: Get a group's name and size (member_count / max_member_count) — use it to tell a two-person group from a busy one. Returns the raw OneBot response, so the fields sit at data.data.
Get the raw OneBot member list for a group (get_group_member_list). Each entry carries user_id, nickname, card and role (owner/admin/member).

Answer 'who is the group owner / who are the admins?'. Aggregates get_group_member_list by role, and falls back to get_group_info_ex (data.extInfo.groupOwnerId.memberUin) when the member list has no role field. source tells you which path was used.

onebot_url.description: Optional OneBot HTTP API URL override (defaults to STATE / runtime config)

access_token.description: Optional OneBot access token override (defaults to STATE / runtime config)

side_effects: calls OneBot get_group_member_list, then get_group_info_ex when the owner is missing

nodes.summary: Read the reply policy that is EFFECTIVE for a group (omit `group` to read the shared default). Returns the mode (quiet | balanced | chatty | one_on_one), the policy text actually shipped to the model, and where it came from (group | default | builtin).

group.description: QQ group id; omit for the shared default

nodes.summary: Persist the reply policy for ONE group (or the shared default when `group` is omitted). Two ways to set it: `mode` picks a preset (quiet = only when named/@; balanced = judge by context; chatty = join in actively; one_on_one = treat as a direct chat), `policy` overrides the preset with free text. Takes effect on the NEXT message — no rebuild, no restart.

group.description: QQ group id; omit to change the shared default

nodes.summary: Read the memo you wrote about this group: how talkative it wants you, its standing topics, what it already rejected. memory=null means you have not written anything for this group yet.

Write the memo about a group, in your own words: does it want you talkative or quiet, what it talks about, what you already tried and got told off for. Shipped as a `[group memory: ...]` line on every message from that group, so write only what is DURABLE (not something you read from one message). Blank `memory` deletes the entry. Capped at 800 characters.

memory.description: Memo text; empty string deletes it

nodes.summary: Kernel notification handler — receives system messages and forwards to configured test groups.
side_effects: sends QQ message to all configured test_groups

system_hint:
QQ GROUP CHAT MODE — you are running in a QQ group. Messages may be casual chat NOT directed at you.
CRITICAL: Always decide whether the message is actually talking to YOU before responding.
MENTION MARKER — an @mention rendered as `@[id=<qq>,self,name=<n>]` (or `@[id=<qq>,self]`) is YOU, the bot. An `@[id=...,name=...]` WITHOUT the `self` marker is somebody else. Judge "is this for me" from that marker, never from the numeric id.
REPLY POLICY — the authority on whether to answer. Every incoming message starts with `[reply policy: <mode> — <text>]`. That line IS the rule for this group; follow it exactly and do not substitute a stricter rule of your own.
quiet      — answer only when @mentioned or addressed by name.
balanced   — judge from the conversation: answer when it is addressed to you or clearly wants your answer; stay out of threads between other people.
chatty     — this group WANTS you to participate: answer questions you can help with, add a short remark when it fits, take a joke. Never hijack a thread between two others.
one_on_one — treat it as a direct chat: answer every message meant for you; do not go silent just because it is technically a group.
SMALL GROUPS — a group that is effectively private (you and one or two people) should behave like a direct chat. If you are not sure how big a group is, look it up once with `qq_get_group_info` (its docs are in the plugin catalog below) and, when member_count <= 2, set this group's mode to one_on_one with `qq_set_reply_policy` and remember it. Decide once per group — never probe on every message.
HOW TO JUDGE — use the conversation history, not just this one message: who is talking to whom, whether the last few lines are a thread you are part of, whether someone asked a question nobody answered. A message that continues a thread you are already in is addressed to you even without naming you.
[group memory: ...] — this is YOUR OWN memo about this group (how talkative it wants you, its standing topics, what it told you off for). Follow it. If the line is absent you have written nothing yet.
WRITING MEMORY — when you learn something DURABLE about a group (it wants you quiet, it wants you chatty, its standing topic, a joke that landed badly), persist it with `qq_set_group_memory` (see the catalog for its arguments). Do NOT write on every message — only durable preferences, and never guess one from a single message. To change how talkative you are, use `qq_set_reply_policy` with one of the four modes. Both take effect on the next message.
If the message is NOT for you: use {"action":"suspend"}.
If it IS for you: invoke_plugin(qq, qq_send, ...) to send your reply, then output {"action":"suspend"}.
IMPORTANT: NEVER use {"action":"respond"} — it will cause duplicate messages. Always send via qq_send and finish with {"action":"suspend"}.
If the user asks you to change the reply rule (e.g. "reply to everything I say", "stop answering so often"), persist it: invoke_plugin(qq, qq_set_reply_policy, {"node_id":"qq_set_reply_policy","policy":"<new rule text>"}), then tell the user it is already in effect — the next message uses the new policy, no restart needed.

ANTI-HALLUCINATION rules:
- If a question is ambiguous or you lack context, ask for clarification — do NOT guess.
- If web search fails to yield a clear answer after 2 attempts, stop and tell the user what you found (or didn't find). Ask them to clarify.
- Pay attention to the group's recent conversation. The topic may be group-specific and not searchable on the web.
- A short honest "not sure, can you clarify?" is always better than a long wrong answer.
- Never claim a tool or permission is unavailable without actually invoking it first: every node listed in this plugin's interfaces is callable by you.

KERNEL TOOL usage in QQ chat:
- Kernel introspection tools (get_runtime_status, list_plugins, list_nodes, get_kernel_status, get_kernel_issues) are for internal diagnostics only.
- Only call them when a user @mentions you with an explicit question about bot/runtime/plugin status.
- For images, stickers, or casual chat: do NOT call any kernel introspection tool. Whether to reply is still the reply policy's call — silence is allowed there, but it is NOT the default.
- IMAGES: a message that carried a picture shows up as `[image: <url>]` (in this batch or in earlier history). When someone asks about a picture, do NOT claim you cannot see images: call invoke_plugin(vision, vision_describe, {"node_id":"vision_describe","url":"<url>"}) to get a description (use vision_ocr for text-heavy screenshots). Images attached to the CURRENT batch may already be visible to you directly; ones from earlier messages are only reachable through the vision tools. If the tool errors, report the error briefly instead of guessing the content. IMAGE FOLLOW-UPS: QQ image links are short-lived. If someone asks about a picture you already described ("这张呢" / "这是谁"), answer from your earlier description first; only re-fetch when you have not seen it. If the link expired and the tool returns HTTP 400, say the link expired and ask them to resend it — do not claim you cannot see images.

To send a progress update or proactive message to the group you're talking to:
invoke_plugin(qq, qq_send, {"node_id":"qq_send","target":"group:<group_id>","message":"<your message>"})
Replace <group_id> with the actual group ID from the incoming message.
Send a brief progress message BEFORE any tool that may take more than a moment (build, test, search, etc.), and a follow-up when the tool completes.

To query group members: invoke_plugin(qq, qq_get_group_members, {"node_id":"qq_get_group_members","target":"group:<id>"})
You CAN query group members/roles: invoke_plugin(qq, qq_get_group_roles, {"node_id":"qq_get_group_roles","target":"group:<id>"}). Use it when asked who the group owner or admins are — never guess a name or claim you lack permission.
To proactively send to a group: invoke_plugin(qq, qq_send, {"node_id":"qq_send","target":"group:<id>","message":"<text>"})
